title: Lesson 8: Reports, Analytics & Mobile
completionTitle: You’re complete! Thanks for finishing the Zoho CRM Training Coach curriculum
coachPersona: You are an experienced OneAccord principal coaching a colleague on reports, analytics and the Zoho CRM (Customer Relationship Management) mobile app. Numbers are only useful if they are visible and honest: dashboards reflect the records people kept. Coach for a two-minute answer to “where do I stand?”, recurring reports that arrive without asking, and logging from the field the moment a meeting ends. In plain, warm, specific language. OneAccord’s values are truth, compassion and service.
keyConcepts: Standard reports and the Report Scheduler
Asking for access through the Zoho admin
Logging from the field with the mobile app
The OneAccord standard, in one page
nextTeaser: That’s the whole Zoho CRM curriculum — revisit any lesson from the menu on the left whenever you need it.

blocks.html:
Last week of the quarter. Your Managing Principal asks: “Where do you stand?” You have an answer, but it takes you forty minutes of opening records to give it — and by the time you finish, one of the deals has moved again.

Same week, you leave a client’s office with three commitments in your head. You mean to log them that evening. At 8 p.m. you remember two of them, and one of those wrong.

Two small failures with the same fix: make the numbers visible before you’re asked, and log from the car park instead of from memory.

blocks.prompt: When someone asks how your pipeline is doing, how much of your answer comes from Zoho and how much from memory? (Optional — skip if you’d rather get started.)
blocks.coachContext: Opening reflection for a lesson on dashboards, scheduled reports and the mobile app. Respond briefly and warmly; connect the learner’s answer to the habit of looking at the same two screens regularly instead of reconstructing from memory.

blocks.html:
By the end of this lesson you’ll be able to:

  1. Answer “where do I stand?” in under two minutes, from your Home tiles and Analytics.
  2. Schedule a recurring report so the numbers arrive without you logging in.
  3. Log from the field with the mobile app, the moment a meeting ends.
  4. Assemble the core habits of this course into one standard you can keep.

About 20 minutes. Have your phone nearby.

Same question, two ways to answer it

From memory and spreadsheetsFrom two screens
Forty minutes opening records one at a time.Home tiles first: open journeys, untouched journeys, calls today, leads.
“I think about three close this month.”Analytics, Org Overview: pipeline by stage, leads this month, projected revenue.
The answer is out of date by the time it’s given.A scheduled report arrives Monday morning whether you ask or not.

The point isn’t the dashboard. It’s that an honest answer takes two minutes, so you’ll actually give it.

1. Where your numbers live

  • Home page tiles: quick glances — My Open Buyer’s Journeys, My Untouched Buyer’s Journeys, My Calls Today, My Leads.
  • Analytics dashboards: fuller views such as Org Overview — leads this month, revenue this month, journeys in pipeline, companies this month, plus charts like leads by source and projected revenue.
  • Standard reports: pre-built lists such as “Buyer’s Journeys closing this month” or “Companies by industry.”

blocks.label: Find it now
blocks.instructions: From the top navigation bar open Analytics and load the Org Overview dashboard (or whichever applies to your role). Note two figures you could quote to your Managing Principal, and one that looks wrong.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve opened a dashboard and noted two useful figures and one doubtful one — continue

blocks.html:
2. Reports that arrive without you

You don’t have to log in to see your numbers. Zoho can email a PDF or Excel version of any report on a schedule — every Monday morning, for example, so the week starts with the facts.

If a report you need is missing, your Profile and Role usually explain it. Raise it with the Zoho admin — Christian or support@oneaccord.co — rather than working around it.

blocks.label: Find it now
blocks.instructions: Open the Reports module, choose one report you would genuinely read weekly, and click New Report Scheduler to set it up for a single weekly send.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve scheduled (or drafted) one recurring report — continue

blocks.html:
3. The mobile app: log before you drive

Much of a principal’s work happens away from a desk. The app exists so the golden rule survives the car park:

  • Calls: make calls from the app, and log calls that reach your mobile straight after they end.
  • Check-in: at a client site, the Check-in button records time and location, so activity reporting is accurate without a separate note.
  • Voice-to-text: dictate outcomes into the record’s Notes section while the details are fresh.
  • Near Me: a map of companies and contacts close by — useful when a meeting ends early.

blocks.label: Action item
blocks.instructions: Open the Zoho CRM app on your phone, find today’s Agenda, and log one real activity from today — a call, a visit or a note — before you close the app.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve logged something real from my phone — continue

blocks.prompt: Where do you find a visual summary of your pipeline?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Analytics holds the dashboards, including Org Overview.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: It’s the Analytics (dashboards) module — that’s where Org Overview and the pipeline charts live.

blocks.prompt: What is the main benefit of the mobile app’s Check-in feature?
options: It schedules your next appointment automatically
It sends a satisfaction survey to the client
It records the time and location of your client meeting for reporting
It advances the Buyer’s Journey stage automatically
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Check-in records time and location so your activity reporting is accurate.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Check-in records the time and location of the client meeting, which keeps activity reporting honest.

blocks.prompt: True or False: you can have Zoho email you a specific report every week, automatically.
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — any report can be scheduled as a recurring PDF or Excel email.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: This one is true — the Report Scheduler sends any report as a recurring PDF or Excel email.

blocks.promptHtml:
It’s the last week of the quarter. Your Managing Principal wants a two-minute answer to “where do you stand?” — and wants to trust it.

Write the routine you would use: which screens you open in which order, what you say first, and what you would check before quoting a number.
rubric: Uses Home tiles for today’s actions and Analytics for the pipeline view, in a stated order
Quotes stage and close-date reality rather than a total, and separates committed from hopeful
Checks anything doubtful in the record before quoting it — stale close dates, missing values, untouched journeys
Keeps the answer to minutes by using a scheduled report rather than rebuilding it by hand
Names at least one thing they would fix in the data as a result of looking
blocks.coachContext: Skill taught: a repeatable two-minute read of Home tiles then Analytics, with verification. Model answer: Home tiles for today’s calls and untouched journeys; Analytics for pipeline by stage and close month; quote committed stages separately from earlier stages; check any journey with a stale close date or no recent activity before quoting; ask for a scheduled weekly report so the routine costs nothing. A good answer ends with a data fix, because dashboards are only as honest as the records.

blocks.promptHtml:
Your dashboard shows four Buyer’s Journeys in pipeline. You know one has gone quiet, one has no close date, and one is at a stage the prospect’s words no longer support.

You’re reporting to your Managing Principal in an hour. Say what you report, what you fix first, and how you explain the difference between the dashboard and the truth.
rubric: Reports the honest picture and explains the gap rather than quoting the dashboard figure
Fixes the data that is wrong — close date, stage correction — before or immediately after reporting
Distinguishes “the number is wrong” from “the deal is weak,” and says which is which
Avoids quietly deleting or downgrading records to make the number look better
Proposes a habit that prevents the same drift — weekly check of untouched journeys
blocks.coachContext: Skill taught: dashboards reflect records, so the analyst’s job is to make them honest. Model answer: report three defensible journeys plus one to be qualified, explain the correction (missing close date, stage moved back on evidence, one journey gone quiet), fix the records, and adopt a weekly pass over untouched journeys. Penalise answers that shade the truth to protect the forecast, and answers that blame the dashboard without correcting it.

blocks.html:
4. The standard, in one page

  • one.zoho.com is your home base, and Zoho CRM is the source of truth: if it isn’t in Zoho, it didn’t happen.
  • Blueprints move every stage of the B.U.Y.E.R.S. pipeline, one honest click at a time.
  • Every stage move needs evidence in the prospect’s own words. Record calls in Teams with consent; quote, don’t paraphrase.
  • Log before you leave: four lines — who, what was decided, what next, by when — and a task for every promise.
  • Look before you’re asked: Home tiles, then Analytics, then a scheduled report on Monday.
  • AI drafts, you decide. Ask for assembly and summaries, verify anything a client will see, and click your own stage buttons.

That’s the course. Everything above is one habit repeated: keep the record true enough that someone else could pick it up.
